result.rationale: Mild activity-related wrist soreness without injury, numbness, or weakness is appropriate for self-care (rest, ergonomic adjustments, wrist positioning, cold/warm compresses). However, ibuprofen and other NSAIDs are generally not recommended during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks, due to fetal kidney and cardiovascular risks; acetaminophen is typically the preferred over-the-counter option in pregnancy. Confirm any medication use with your prenatal provider, and seek care if you develop numbness, tingling, weakness, worsening pain, or swelling.
